item.title: Authenticating Meshery via CLI
item.description:
mesheryctl needs a token to call Meshery Server on your behalf. Run mesheryctl system login to get one. Meshery Server must be running first, so start it with mesheryctl system start if it is not.

Log in from a machine with a browser

  1. Run the login command:

    mesheryctl system login

    mesheryctl asks Meshery Server which providers it offers and prompts you to pick one:

    Use the arrow keys to navigate: ↓ ↑ → ←
? Select a Provider:
 ▸ Meshery
 Local

    The list comes from your server, so it shows any additional remote providers your server is configured with. To skip the prompt, name the provider with -p, for example mesheryctl system login -p Meshery. Run mesheryctl system provider list to see the names.

item.title: Configuring Autocompletion for `mesheryctl`
item.description:
mesheryctl completion prints a completion script for bash, zsh, or fish. Load that script in your shell so that pressing Tab completes mesheryctl commands and flags.

Bash

Check your bash version with bash --version, then use the matching commands.

Linux, bash 4.0 or later

Load completion in the current shell:

source <(mesheryctl completion bash)

To load it in every new shell, add that line to ~/.bashrc.

item.title: Mesheryctl system commands
item.description:
mesheryctl system commands manage the Meshery deployment described by your current context. The commands follow the pattern mesheryctl system <command> [subcommand] [flags]. Every system command also accepts:

  • -c, --context <name> to act on a different context for this one command.
  • -y, --yes to answer yes to every confirmation prompt, which is useful in scripts.

This page shows the commands you use most. For every flag, see the mesheryctl system reference.

Start, stop, and restart Meshery

start

mesheryctl system start deploys Meshery to the platform in your current context and opens Meshery UI in your default browser.

item.title: Running mesheryctl in a CI Pipeline
item.description:
Use this guide to run mesheryctl from a CI job, such as a GitHub Actions workflow, a GitLab pipeline, or a Jenkins agent. A CI runner has no browser and nobody to answer prompts, so you install a pinned mesheryctl, give it a token, and pass flags that skip every prompt. The examples use GitHub Actions, but each step is a shell command that works on any runner.

Before you begin

  • A runner with bash, curl, and jq. To start Meshery on the runner itself, the runner also needs Docker, or access to a Kubernetes cluster.
  • A way to authenticate. Choose one:
    • A Remote Provider token, if your pipeline works with your organization’s designs, environments, or performance results. Download it from Meshery Cloud as described in Log in from a machine without a browser, and store the value of its token key as a CI secret. The examples use a secret named MESHERY_TOKEN.
    • The Local provider, if the pipeline starts a throwaway Meshery Server and needs nothing from your organization. It needs no secret.

item.title: Running system checks using Meshery CLI
item.description:
mesheryctl system check verifies that your machine is ready to deploy Meshery and that an existing Meshery deployment is healthy. Run it before you deploy Meshery, and again whenever Meshery misbehaves.

Run mesheryctl system check --help to see every flag, or see the mesheryctl system check reference.

Check your machine before you deploy

Run the pre-deployment checks with --preflight (or its alias --pre):

mesheryctl system check --preflight

item.title: Using Meshery CLI
item.description:
mesheryctl is Meshery’s command line interface. Use it to manage the lifecycle of Meshery itself and to call Meshery’s infrastructure management features from your terminal. Its commands fall into these groups:

  • mesheryctl - global flags (--config, --verbose), version, and completion
  • mesheryctl system - Meshery lifecycle, contexts, providers, tokens, and troubleshooting
  • mesheryctl design - design import, export, deployment, and evaluation
  • mesheryctl model - model management and registry operations
  • mesheryctl component - component lookup
  • mesheryctl relationship - relationship management
  • mesheryctl registry - capability registry generation and publishing
  • mesheryctl connection - connection management
  • mesheryctl environment - environment management
  • mesheryctl workspace - workspace management
  • mesheryctl organization - organization management
  • mesheryctl filter - WebAssembly filter management
  • mesheryctl perf - performance management
  • mesheryctl adapter - Meshery Adapter operations
  • mesheryctl exp - experimental commands

Configure Meshery deployments with meshconfig

Meshconfig is the mesheryctl configuration file at ~/.meshery/config.yaml. It holds one or more contexts, and each context describes one Meshery deployment. mesheryctl system commands such as start, stop, status, and reset act on the current context.
